ce_bugs.text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:491 — Because created video references now lack credentialId (see EventManager.ts:170), `if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)` fails and deleteMeeting is skipped, leaving the remote video meeting (Zoom/Google Meet/etc.) undeleted on cancellation

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 — Calendar.createEvent` interface now takes `credentialId`, but only GoogleCalendarService uses it to pick the matching destinationCalendar entry — Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`) still just use the first ("main host") destinationCalendar regardless of which host/credential is creating the event, so multi-host routing silently only works for Google Calendar

mrv_findings.text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-119 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is `[]`/null (now a common state), regressing the old safe `?.integration` access. (P0, confidence 100)

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125, office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:125 vs googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:87 — only Google's `createEvent` implements the new `credentialId` param; Lark/Office365/iCal still use `destinationCalendar[0]` unconditionally, so every host's event is created in the first host's calendar for non-Google providers — the core multi-host bug is fixed for only 1 of 4 providers with no compiler error. (P0/P1, confidence 90)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1077-1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when destinationCalendar is `null` (organizer has none configured), silently dropping all other collective hosts' calendars. (P1, confidence 85)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256,315-317 — `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is already falsy, so it searches for externalId===undefined which never matches — dead fallback, breaks per-host calendar targeting on update/delete. (P1, confidence 85)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — `booking.references.find(...)` (singular) was missed when converting the merge/reschedule stale-event cleanup path to multi-reference; only one arbitrary host's old calendar event gets deleted on reschedule/merge, leaving orphaned duplicates for other hosts. (P2, confidence 75)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339-374 — `createAllCalendarEvents` does sequential unbatched `prisma.credential.findUnique` per host inside the loop instead of a batched `findMany`/parallel fetch (N+1); also destinations without `credentialId` sharing the same `integration` type can create duplicate calendar events. (P2, confidence 70/60)

packages/core/EventManager.ts + handleCancelBooking.ts — DB credential-fetch fallback (`prisma.credential.findUnique`) duplicated in 3 places, breaking EventManager's constructor-scoped-credentials boundary by reaching into Prisma directly inside business-logic loops, with fetched credentials never revalidated against the `_calendar` type invariant. (P2, confidence 70)
